deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 6% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 10.0% = 10-year Treasury 5.0% + 5%; base: last 12 months of free cash flow). For comparison, sales grew 27% last year; 12%/yr over 3 years — the market expects a slowdown from its recent pace.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 7% (3 years ago 3%, rising) — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $7 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 11% (3 years ago 5%).

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $10.9B, up 8% from a year ago — about 26% of the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $5.6B, up 5% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 12%/yr over 3 years and 9%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 6% vs a 5-year range of -1–7% (median 4%): near the top of a fairly narrow range.
deeper.margin_position: near the top of a fairly narrow range

deeper.title: Cash returned to shareholders
deeper.text: Returned $1.3B to shareholders over the last 12 months ($547M buybacks + $739M dividends) = 2.0% of the company's market value. Share count up 2.0% from a year ago (stock pay outpacing buybacks — dilution).

deeper.title: Analyst estimates
deeper.text: Next year's earnings-per-share estimate $4.74, up 17% in 90 days (up 1% in the last 30); 12 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. This year's earnings-per-share estimate $3.83, up 12% in 90 days; 2 analysts raised, 0 cut in 30 days. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

deeper.title: Where sales come from
deeper.text: By segment, latest quarter vs a year earlier: Cloud & AI 74% of sales, up 25%; Networking 24% of sales, up 75%; Data Center Networking 3% of sales, up 112%. Source: 10-Q XBRL.

tiles.title: Earnings per share
tiles.sub: +108% vs a year ago · $1.93 over 12 months (GAAP)
tiles.read: Profit per share grew 108% vs sales 34% (latest quarter vs a year earlier): profits are outgrowing sales, so margins are widening.
tiles.explain: EPS = profit divided by the number of shares. The quarterly figures are the 'adjusted' EPS analysts track (Yahoo); the 12-month figure is the official GAAP number from SEC filings.

tiles.title: Earnings vs forecasts
tiles.sub: last 8 reports · bars = EPS beat (+) or miss (−) vs the average forecast
tiles.read: Beat forecasts 5 quarters running, by growing margins (6% → 18%): analysts keep underestimating it.
tiles.explain: A 'beat' means reported EPS came in above the average analyst forecast. Source: Yahoo (unofficial).

tiles.title: Sales growth
tiles.sub: latest quarter +34% vs a year earlier · 12-month sales $41.9B
tiles.read: Latest quarter: sales up 34% vs a year earlier and speeding up (from 18% two quarters ago): demand is strengthening.
tiles.explain: Headline: sales over the last 12 months vs the 12 months before. Bars: each quarter's sales vs the same quarter a year earlier.

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $6 of operating profit, up from $1 a year ago: profitability is improving.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: It turned 149% of its reported profit into spare cash: the profits are real money, not just accounting.
tiles.explain: Free cash flow = cash from operations minus spending on equipment and buildings: money the company could return or reinvest.

tiles.title: Price vs profits (P/E)
tiles.read: You pay 23× last year's profit (higher than 83% of the last 5 years); only 10× next year's forecast, so the market expects profits to jump.
tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.

tiles.title: Next earnings
tiles.read: Reports Nov 23; analysts expect EPS of $1.28, up 106% from a year ago. It usually moves about 7% the day after, so expect a swing.
tiles.explain: Consensus = the average analyst forecast (Yahoo, unofficial). The typical move is the average size of the stock's next-day move after its last reports, not an options-implied figure.
